quiz.q: Why capture headers, query params and the original payload into variables at the start of the request?
options: Connectors like HTTP Request overwrite payload and attributes, but variables persist
quiz.explain: Variables aren't overwritten unless you deliberately do it, so the values stay available for logging, mapping and calling other systems.

quiz.q: The class puts the initial-variables step in the main flow before the APIkit Router. Which value will be empty there?
quiz.explain: Before routing, URI parameters aren't extracted yet (the Listener path is /api/*). The class captured attributes.uriParams.empid inside the resource flows instead.

quiz.q: Why is the initial-variables logic a sub flow called via Flow Reference?
options: It only creates variables and needs no source or error handling of its own
Only sub flows can use Transform Message
Private flows can't be called before the router
quiz.explain: A sub flow has no source and no error handling, which fits a step that just sets variables.

quiz.q: A query-param variable's value depends on a URI-param variable. Can both be created in the same Transform Message?
options: No — create the first, then the dependent one in a later component
quiz.explain: One Transform Message with several targets works only when the variables are independent.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of JSON Logger over the plain Logger?
options: It has a global connector configuration applied to every logger in the project
It removes the need for log levels
quiz.explain: With the plain Logger every logger must be filled manually with IDs; JSON Logger's global config applies to all loggers. It's a custom connector shared via Exchange.

quiz.q: In JSON Logger, what does setting indent = false do?
options: Prints the JSON on a single line — less readable but lightweight
quiz.explain: Indent defaults to true (multi-line, readable); false gives a single line.

quiz.q: You copy a logger that uses flow.name into another flow. What does it print?
options: The name of the flow it's now in
quiz.explain: flow.name gives the current flow's name, so copied loggers report the right flow automatically. app.name gives the app's name.

quiz.q: Which trace point fits a logger placed just before a Database Insert?
quiz.explain: BEFORE_REQUEST/AFTER_REQUEST surround external calls; the class used BEFORE_DB and AFTER_DB.

quiz.q: How do you reference the transaction-id header stored in vars.headers in DataWeave?
quiz.explain: Keys with hyphens must be quoted; otherwise DataWeave treats the hyphen as a minus sign.

quiz.q: Your app runs on CloudHub and logs now(). Which time zone does it use by default?
quiz.explain: now() uses the server's time zone; locally that's your laptop, on CloudHub it's UTC by default.

quiz.q: Don't many loggers slow down a Mule API?
options: Yes — each logger blocks until written
No significant impact — logging is asynchronous and written in the background
quiz.explain: The flow hands the message to the logger and moves on, like sending pages to a printer queue.

quiz.q: Why must data like Aadhaar, PAN, mobile numbers and salary not appear in full in logs?
options: They can be misused, and regulators such as the RBI can audit production logs
quiz.explain: Sensitive information must be masked (e.g. show only the last 4 digits) using DataWeave's mask function, covered next session.

cards.front: Why capture headers and params into variables at the start?
cards.back: Connectors overwrite payload and attributes; variables persist through the flow.

cards.front: Where to create common initial variables?
cards.back: Once, in the main flow **before the APIkit Router** (via a sub flow) — but URI params are only available after routing.
Sub flow with one Transform Message setting `queryParams`, `uriParams`, `headers`, `startTime`, `requestPayload`; payload untouched.
Fallback value when an expression is null, e.g. `attributes.queryParams default ""`.
One Transform Message with several targets, several Set Variables, or one object variable (e.g. `vars.originalRequest.queryParams`). No right or wrong.
If one variable depends on another, create them in separate components.
Custom connector producing structured JSON logs, with a global configuration applied to every logger.
Connector built by an organisation and shared via **Exchange** — build once, reuse many times.

cards.front: Why JSON Logger over the default Logger?
cards.back: Structured JSON, global config, trace points, consistent fields (correlation/transaction IDs), masking support.
Default **true** = pretty multi-line JSON; **false** = single line, lightweight.
INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ERROR, TRACE. Default is INFO; DEBUG prints only if that category is set to DEBUG (e.g. in log4j2.xml).
Current application / flow names — copied loggers report the right flow automatically.
START, END, BEFORE_REQUEST, AFTER_REQUEST (class: BEFORE_DB / AFTER_DB), FLOW.
At START and END of processing and **before/after every external call**.
Quote them: `vars.headers.'transaction-id'`; otherwise the hyphen is a minus sign.
DataWeave function returning the current date-time (with milliseconds) of the server.
**UTC** by default.
Set `startDbTime = now()` before the call; after it, `now() - vars.startDbTime`.
The flow hands the message to the logger and moves on; writing happens in the background (printer-queue analogy).
RollingFile appender to `<app>.log`, 10 MB size trigger, max 10 rollovers; `AsyncRoot` at INFO.
Data that must not be exposed: Aadhaar, PAN, mobile, salary, card numbers, email IDs.

cards.front: Why mask sensitive data in logs?
cards.back: To prevent misuse and meet regulatory/audit requirements (e.g. RBI audits of production logs).
Hiding part of a value (e.g. show only the last 4 digits). DataWeave has a `mask` function.
